settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic pricing with limited supply (regret w.r.t. fixed-price benchmark)
unmapped: posted-price auction: action is a price p in [0,1], agent with i.i.d. valuation from unknown F buys iff v >= p; only the binary sale decision is observed (which determines the revenue)
supply constraint: at most k items (B) can be sold over n agents (T); the process stops once k items are sold
regret against best fixed-price strategy A_k^n(p) which itself respects the supply limit
settings.definition_quote: A seller has $k$ items she can sell to a set of $n$ agents ... The private values are independently drawn from the same {\em demand distribution} $F$ ... unknown to the seller ... $\mathtt{support}(F)\subset [0,1]$ ... $\Regret(\A) \triangleq \max_p \Payoff[\A_k^n(p)] - \Payoff(\A)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic pricing with limited supply (regret w.r.t. offline benchmark / Myerson auction)
unmapped: posted-price auction with binary sale feedback and k-item supply limit
benchmark is the optimal offline (Myerson) mechanism that knows F and is not restricted to posted prices
settings.definition_quote: Our main benchmark is the maximal expected revenue of an offline mechanism that is allowed to use the demand distribution; henceforth, we will call it \emph{offline benchmark}.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: There exists a detail-free pricing strategy such that for any regular demand distribution its expected revenue is at least the offline benchmark minus $O((k \log n)^{2/3})$.

results.notes: k items = B, n agents = T. Comparator is the optimal offline Myerson mechanism (mapped to best_policy). Follows from Theorem 1.2 plus Yan's benchmark lemma.

tuning: alpha = Theta(log n) in confidence radius

source.label: thm:main-fixed
source.quote: There exists a detail-free pricing strategy whose expected revenue is at least the fixed-price benchmark minus $O((k \log n)^{2/3})$. This result holds for every demand distribution. Moreover, this result is the best possible up to a factor of $O(\log n)$.

results.notes: Same statement as Lemma 4.3 (CappedUCB with delta = k^{-1/3}(log n)^{2/3} achieves regret O(k log n)^{2/3}). No assumption on F. Comparator is the best fixed-price strategy respecting supply.

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: No detail-free pricing strategy can achieve regret $o(k^{2/3})$ for arbitrarily large $k,n$.

results.notes: Statement is 'not o(k^{2/3})', i.e. an infinitely-often Omega(k^{2/3}) lower bound; proved by reduction to the unlimited-supply lower bound of Kleinberg-Leighton.

conditions: constant c_F may depend on F

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: For any $\gamma<\tfrac12$, no detail-free pricing strategy can achieve regret $O(c_F\, k^\gamma)$ for all demand distributions $F$ and arbitrarily large $k,n$, where the constant $c_F$ can depend on $F$.

results.notes: Also stated as Theorem 1.5. Expressed as: regret with distribution-dependent constant cannot be O(c_F k^gamma) for gamma<1/2.

symbols.c_F: distribution-dependent constant, c_F = 1 + 1/g'(s_F) with g(s) = s S^{-1}(s)
symbols.s_F: distribution-dependent positive constant; s_F = 1/4 for MHR distributions

source.label: thm:improved-regret
source.quote: For any regular demand distribution $F$ there exist positive constants $s_F$ and $c_F$ such that $\UCBcap$ with parameter $\delta = k^{-1/2}\,\log(n)$ achieves regret $O(c_F\,\sqrt{k}\log n)$ whenever $\fkn\leq s_F$. For monotone hazard rate distributions we can take $s_F = \tfrac{1}{4}$.

source.label: thm:MHR-intro
source.quote: There exists a detail-free pricing strategy whose expected revenue, for any regular demand distribution $F$, is  at least the offline benchmark minus $O(c_F\, \sqrt{k} \log n)$ whenever $\fkn\leq s_F$, where $c_F$ and $s_F$ are positive constants that depend on $F$. For monotone hazard rate distributions one can take $s_F = \tfrac14$.

results.notes: Offline benchmark version; combines Theorem 5.2 with Yan's O(sqrt k) benchmark gap.

symbols.g_prime: g'(k/n), derivative of g(s) = s S^{-1}(s) at k/n

source.label: thm:improved-regret-trade-off
source.quote: For each $\gamma\in [\tfrac13, \tfrac12]$, consider pricing strategy $\UCBcap$ with parameter $\delta = \tilde{O}(k^{-\gamma})$. This pricing strategy achieves regret $\tilde{O}(k^{1-\gamma}) (1+1/g'(\fkn))$ if the demand distribution is regular and $g'(\fkn)>0$, and regret $\tilde{O}(k^{2\gamma})$ for arbitrary demand distributions.

results.notes: Regular-distribution branch of the trade-off theorem.

source.label: thm:improved-regret-trade-off
source.quote: ... and regret $\tilde{O}(k^{2\gamma})$ for arbitrary demand distributions.

results.notes: Arbitrary-distribution branch of the trade-off theorem.

conditions: demand distribution F has monotone hazard rate
tuning: delta = (log(k)/k)^{1/4} (up to log log factors per Lemma 7.3)

source.label: thm:descending
source.quote: For some parameters $\epsilon$ and $\delta$, Mechanism~\ref{alg:pp} achieves regret $O\left({k^{3/4}\poly\log(k)} \right) $ with respect to the offline benchmark, for any demand distribution that satisfies the monotone hazard rate condition.

results.notes: Also Theorem 1.6. Polylog is in k only (no dependence on n); recorded as O_tilde. Derived from multiplicative Lemma 7.3 (revenue >= (1-O(delta)) of offline benchmark), not recorded separately.
